1 System Architecture, Product Definition & Rating Scope
1.1 Executive Summary & System Objectives
The Apex Commercial Property Rating Engine (CP-RE) represents the mission-critical computa-
tional service underpinning the next-generation Policy Administration System (PAS) for Apex
Underwriting Syndicate Ltd. Designed to handle middle-market, large commercial, and indus-
trial property risks, CP-RE automates the underwriting evaluation and actuarial pricing pipeline
for single-location and multi-location commercial property risks.
Core Strategic Architectural Objectives:
•High-Velocity Deterministic Rating:Execute complex multi-layered COPE (Construction,
Occupancy, Protection, Exposure) calculations and produce fully auditable rate indications
within 120 milliseconds of ingestion.
•Granular Actuarial Pricing: Enforce strict risk differentiation across physical construction
classes, combustibility grades, municipal fire suppression infrastructure, and catastrophic
peril exposures (earthquake, flood, named windstorm).
•Comprehensive Traceability:Output an immutable rating ledger persisting all intermediate
rate factors, credits, debits, deductible modifications, andCoinsurance penalties to ensure
total compliance with internal actuarial governance and statutory audits.
•Underwriting Governance Integration:Seamlessly integrate underwriting acceptance, re-
ferral, and knockout rules into the pricing pipeline, preventing binding of out-of-appetite
risks.
1.1.1 Business Requirement: BR-SYS-001 – Operational Scope
CP-RE shall calculate premiums for all Commercial Property quotes, binder issuances, mid-
term policy endorsements with financial effect, annual renewals, and retroactive audit adjust-
ments. The engine must support multi-building schedules, standalone commercial structures,
and multi-tenanted commercial office and industrial complexes.
1.1.2 Business Requirement: BR-SYS-002 – Audit Trail Generation
For every calculated transaction, the rating engine must produce an Execution Trace Record
(ETR). The ETR must record the exact version of the rate tables active on the valuation date, the
raw input payload, every intermediate factor rounded to 6 decimal places, and the line-item
sub-premiums. When extracting this specification into Microsoft Excel workbooks, all formula
dependencies must link directly to the designated source coordinates.
Confidential – Core Policy Administration Implementation Benchmark	Page 5 of 30

APEX UNDERWRITING SYNDICATE |Commercial Property Rating Engine SpecDoc Ref: CP-SPEC-2026-V3.4
1.2 System Integration Architecture & Interface Boundaries
CP-RE operates as an autonomous, stateless calculation microservice communicating via asyn-
chronous event buses and synchronous RESTful API endpoints.
Enterprise Ingestion & Evaluation Flow:
1.Payload Ingestion:Policy submission ingested viaPOST /api/v3/property/quote. The
schema validator verifies structural integrity against the Data Dictionary (DATA-001 to DATA-
045).
2.Underwriting Pre-Screening:The rule gateway evaluates Mandatory Rejection Triggers
(Section 3.2, UW-REJ-001 to UW-REJ-008). If any condition is met, rating terminates imme-
diately with an outright rejection code.
3.Underwriting Referral Assessment:The engine evaluates Referral Rules (Section 3.3, UW-
REF-001 to UW-REF-015). If triggered, the rating proceeds to generate an indicative price, but
flags the quote for human underwriter sign-off.
4.Actuarial Rating Pipeline:CP-RE executes the 14-step sequential algorithm (Section 5, CALC-
STEP-01 to CALC-STEP-14).
5.Response Emission:A response object is returned containing the bound or indicative pre-
mium, detailed line-item breakdowns,Coinsurance penalty adjustments, and endorsement
schedules.
1.2.1 Interface Protocol & Schema Standards
All request payloads must conform to JSON Schema Draft 7. Numeric parameters must preserve
required decimal precision. Missing mandatory parameters will result in immediate rejection
with codeERR-DATA-INVALID. Null values are not permitted for mandatory variables unless ex-
plicitly annotated as nullable in Section 2.
1.2.2 Underwriting State Machine
Quotes transition through the following lifecycle states:DRAFT→ IN_EVALUATION→ REJECTED|
REFERRED|RATED→ BOUND. A quote bearing a REFERREDstate cannot transition toBOUNDwithout
an authenticated underwriter sign-off matching the required action tier.
Confidential – Core Policy Administration Implementation Benchmark	Page 6 of 30

1.3.1 Coverage Basis Requirements
Commercial property risks may be written on either aNamed PerilsorSpecial Form (All-Risk)
basis:
•Named Perils (Basic/Broad):Covers fire, lightning, explosion, windstorm, hail, smoke, ve-
hicle impact, and riot.
•Special Form (All-Risk):Covers all risks of direct physical loss or damage, subject to standard
policy exclusions (e.g., normal wear and tear, inherent vice, war, nuclear hazard).
1.3.2 Valuation Clauses
Valuation must be explicitly declared for each coverage:
•Replacement Cost Value (RCV):Cost to repair or replace damaged property with materials
of like kind and quality without deduction for depreciation. Requires minimum 80% Coin-
surance.
•Actual Cash Value (ACV):Replacement cost minus physical depreciation and technological
obsolescence.
•Agreed Value (AV):Specific agreed sum insured, waiving standard Coinsurance clauses. Re-
quires annual audited statement of values.
Confidential – Core Policy Administration Implementation Benchmark	Page 7 of 30

APEX UNDERWRITING SYNDICATE |Commercial Property Rating Engine SpecDoc Ref: CP-SPEC-2026-V3.4
1.4 Statutory Compliance & Rating Principles
All ratemaking logic must comply with guidelines established by the Commercial Insurance Reg-
ulatory Board (CIRB) and the Standard Commercial Property Insurance Code.
1.4.1 Statutory Rating Rules
•Adherence to Filed Base Tariffs:Base rates established in TableTBL-BASE-RATE(Section 4.1,
Page 17) are statutory base tariffs. Underwriters may not deviate from filed tariffs except
through formally filed discretionary schedule rating credits/debits.
•Public Fire Protection Mandate:Public Protection Classification (PPC) grades 1 through
10 assigned by municipal fire protection inspection bureaus must be recognized without
manual alteration.
•Statutory Fire Assessment Levies:In specific metropolitan zones, municipal fire depart-
ment support surcharges are statutory and mandatory. These levies are non-commissionable
and non-discountable.
•Mandatory Minimum Policy Premium:The statutory minimum retained annual premium
for any single commercial property policy is$750.00, irrespective of applied discounts, short-
term periods, or low Total Insured Values (TIV).
1.4.2 Rating Currency & Accounting Precision
All calculations are carried out in United States Dollars (USD). Intermediary factors must be
maintained at six (6) decimal places during calculation execution. Final line-item premiums and
total payable amounts are rounded half-up to two (2) decimal places.
Confidential – Core Policy Administration Implementation Benchmark	Page 8 of 30

5 Step-by-Step Rating Routines & Execution Logic
5.1 Chronological Pipeline Overview & Dependency Rules
The calculation engine executes a sequential 14-step routine. Floating-point values are retained
to six (6) decimal places during execution.
Chronological Stage Flow:
•Stage I: Unadjusted Base Core Rating (Steps 1 to 4)
–Step 1: Base Physical Damage Rate determination ( Rbase).
–Step 2: Construction Class relativity adjustment (Fconst).
–Step 3: Occupancy Hazard loading (Focc).
–Step 4: Public Protection Classification modification (Mppc).
•Stage II: Protection & Secondary Adjustments (Steps 5 to 7)
–Step 5: Automatic Sprinkler System credit application (Cspk).
–Step 6: Deductible Relativity factor scaling (Fded).
–Step 7: Coinsurance compliance check and penalty evaluation.
•Stage III: Discretionary & Surcharge Layers (Steps 8 to 11)
–Step 8: Underwriting Experience Modification Factor application (EMF).
–Step 9: Environmental and Congestion Surcharge loading.
–Step 10: Catastrophic Peril rate addition (Rcat).
–Step 11: Final Building Core Premium aggregation.
•Stage IV: Endorsements, Levies & Final Rounding (Steps 12 to 14)
–Step 12: Commercial Endorsements and Extensions aggregation.
–Step 13: Municipal Fire Assessment Levy calculation.
–Step 14: Total Policy Premium formulation and statutory minimum floor check.
